rationale: M60 R10 sibling pin. groovy builds an override endpoint the same way java does (`${ownerFqn}.${name}${signature}`, buildFqn + resolveOverrides), so the parameter list is inside the string the edge label is derived from, and its pre-fix rule cut at the FIRST '(' before splitting on dots — immune to a qualified-parameter split, but truncating a paren-bearing owner chain. Both lanes now call one shared rule (src/ast/override-context.ts localEdgeLabel). MEASURED INTERACTION, recorded rather than smoothed over: on this fixture the groovy signature reads `(Entity,,StringBuilder,boolean)` — the WRITTEN qualified type `Outer.Criterion` is recorded as absent, so the label defect this fixture guards cannot currently fire in this lane. That payload loss is a separate, measured finding with its own instrument (script/m60/groovy-parameter-payload-census.ts: 8 of 33 joined written-qualified slots record no type on a 600-file grails-core sample; root cause probe-verified — the grammar uses `scoped_type_identifier` for such a type and the parameter extractor's node list does not name it). When that is fixed, the forbid below becomes live, which is why it is pinned now.

forbidRelationships.note: java's pre-fix derivation on this signature once the parameter payload keeps the written qualified type — not a name, owner lost. Vacuous today only because the type is dropped; the pin is for the day it is not.
